correctness.rationale: The graph is the Cartesian product of the star and P_2, with a shared spine edge and no edges between distinct pages away from the spine. With no spine selected, an empty page is undominated and a singleton is unmatched, so all pages must be full. With only a selected, domination or matchability forces every x_i to be selected, and exactly one x_i can lack its partner y_i: it must match a, and parity requires it. The reflected case uses b. With both spine vertices selected, domination is automatic and a singleton page can match only its corresponding spine vertex; hence there is at most one of each orientation, and parity permits only zero or two. The constructive matchings in all admissible states verify sufficiency. This counts sets, not matchings. The contributions are x^2(1+x^2)^n, n(n-1)x^4(1+x^2)^{n-2}, 2n x^{2n}, and x^{2n}; n=2 gives x^2+9x^4+x^6. Thus the spine is the unique minimum for n>=2, and evaluating at one gives the claimed total. For n=1 each of the four edges of C_4 gives a paired dominating set, as does the full graph. The frozen verification description and finite checker were read without executing it.

originality.rationale: There is demonstrable full coverage in a distinct indexed theorem: the quadrilateral-books result states the identical all-set polynomial for every n>=2 and proves the equivalent four-class census. It also gives a refined inclusion-minimal classification that the frozen record does not claim. This is a finding about exact coverage in the checked corpus, not a claim that the later-dated record was available first, that the frozen record derived from it, or that the result was known at the time of the frozen record. The unresolved 2016 source is not a reason for failure.
residual_risks: Historical provenance and priority are unresolved; the exact equivalent indexed statement is later-dated. No inference of derivation is made.
The scope of the 2016 paired-domination polynomial paper remains unverified; its inaccessibility does not decide originality.
